workflow.name: Trigger HVAC upsell campaigns from weather data and handle bookings with GoHighLevel, WhatsApp, WeatherAPI and Gemini
workflow.description:
# Project Overview: Automated Climate-Driven HVAC Upsell & AI Concierge

This project is specifically built for an HVAC business to automatically upsell to old customers when their locality has a heatwave or snow wave forecast in the upcoming five days.

## Prerequisites & Setup

### 1. GoHighLevel (GHL)

* **Create Custom Fields:**
* `stop_whatsapp`: Used when a user replies "STOP" to remove them from the marketing list.
* `opp_type`: To track the campaign type (e.g., *heatwave* or *snowwave*).


* **Create Two Pipelines:**
* Pipeline A: **HEATWAVE**
* Pipeline B: **SNOWWAVE**
* *Note:* Both pipelines require 4 stages: **New Lead**, **Contacted**, **Scheduled**, and **Closed**.


* **Grab the Calendar ID:** Keep your GHL Calendar ID handy, as the workflow will need it to search for free slots and book appointments.

### 2. WhatsApp (Meta Business Suite)

Create and approve two marketing templates for proactive outreach:

**A. Heatwave Template**

> Hello {{1}},
> With temperatures expected to rise soon, we wanted to share a few tips to keep your home comfortable and your AC running efficiently.
> **Maintenance Tips:**
> • Keep blinds closed during peak sun hours.
> • Check your air filters; a clean filter prevents overworking.
> • If you leave the house, raise the thermostat a few degrees rather than turning it off.
> **Need help?**
> If your system is struggling to keep up, we are here to assist.
> Stay cool and safe!

**B. Snow Wave Template**

> Hello {{1}},
> With a cold front and freezing temperatures expected soon, we wanted to share a few tips to keep your home warm and your heating system running efficiently.
> **Winter Comfort Tips:**
> • Keep curtains and blinds open during the day to let sunlight naturally warm your home, then close them at night to trap the heat.
> • Check your air filters; a clogged filter makes your heater work much harder in freezing weather.
> • Ensure your outdoor vents and heat pump units are clear of snow or debris to maintain proper airflow.
> **Need help?**
> If your heating system is struggling to stay warm or making unusual noises, we are here to assist.
> Stay warm and safe!

### 3. API Integrations

* **Nominatim OpenStreetMap API:** Review the documentation. This open-source tool will be used to extract exact cities from customer street addresses.
* **WeatherAPI:** Obtain a free API key. Add this to your workflow's generic credentials (Type: `Query Auth` > Name: `key` > Value: `your-api-key`).
* **Gemini API:** Obtain your API key to power the AI Service Concierge.

---

## Part 1: The Climate-Driven Lead Generation Engine (Proactive Outreach)

This sub-workflow acts as a proactive scraper. It monitors your CRM contacts, cross-references their locations with live weather data, and triggers targeted upsell campaigns.

**1. Schedule Trigger & Fetch Contacts**

* **Schedule Trigger:** Kicks off the workflow every morning at 7:00 AM.
* **Fetch Contacts (HighLevel):** Pulls your entire list of previous customers and leads from GoHighLevel.

**2. Geocoding & Data Cleaning**

* **If Node (City Set):** Checks if the CRM contact already has a city populated.
* **Nominatim API (Loop & Fetch):** If a city is missing, the workflow runs the address through the Nominatim OpenStreetMap API to extract the exact city.
* **Update Contact (HighLevel):** Saves the extracted city back to the GHL contact profile to prevent redundant geocoding in the future.

**3. Weather Data Aggregation**

* **Code Node (Group by City):** A vital step to optimize API usage. Instead of making 1,000 separate calls for 1,000 contacts, custom JavaScript groups all contacts by their respective cities.
* **HTTP Request (Fetch Forecast):** Pings WeatherAPI.com to grab the 5-day forecast for each unique city.

**4. Hazard Detection & Routing**

* **Code Node (Detect Weather Hazards):** A script evaluates the 5-day forecast against dynamic, seasonal temperature thresholds (e.g., a "heatwave" threshold in May might be >85°F, but >95°F in August). It tags the grouped contacts with a campaign type (`HEATWAVE` or `SNOWWAVE`).
* **If Node (Check Campaign Type):** Routes the qualified leads into the appropriate pipeline logic.

**5. CRM Execution & WhatsApp Outreach**

* **Create Opportunity (HighLevel):** Drops the qualified lead into the "New Lead" stage of the respective GHL pipeline.
* **Send Template (WhatsApp):** Dispatches the pre-approved Meta marketing template to the customer.
* **Update & Upsert (HighLevel):** Moves the Opportunity to the "Contacted" stage and updates the `opp_type` custom field so the system tracks the reason for outreach.

---

## Part 2: The AI-Powered Service Concierge (Inbound Handling)

When a customer replies to the proactive blast (e.g., *"My AC is making a weird noise, can someone come out?"*), this sub-workflow seamlessly takes over to assist the customer and autonomously book an appointment.

**1. Trigger & Validation**

* **Trigger (WhatsApp Message Received):** Listens for inbound replies from customers.
* **Fetch & Validate (HighLevel):** Looks up the sender's phone number in GHL. If the number does not exist in the CRM, the workflow ignores the message to prevent spam handling.

**2. The Opt-Out Filter**

* **If Node (Stop Command):** Scans the inbound message for the keyword "STOP".
* **Upsert Contact (HighLevel):** If "STOP" is detected, the workflow immediately updates the user's `stop_whatsapp` custom field to `TRUE`, excluding them from all future blasts, and terminates the flow.

**3. The Agentic Core**

* **Customer Service AI Agent (LangChain + Gemini):** If the user is requesting assistance, the message is routed to an AI Agent powered by the Gemini Chat Model.
* **Redis Chat History Memory:** Connects to a Redis instance so the AI retains conversation context, which is crucial for natural, back-and-forth scheduling.
* **Agent Tools (HighLevel Integration):** The Gemini agent is equipped with specific tools it can trigger autonomously:
* *Fetch Available Calendar Slots:* The AI is strictly instructed to check live GHL availability before suggesting times to the user.
* *Book Calendar Appointment:* Automatically secures the timeslot in GHL if the user agrees.
* *Close Deal:* If the user declines service (*"I'm good, no thanks"*), the AI triggers this tool to mark the GHL opportunity as "Closed/Lost".
* *Update Pipeline Stage:* If an appointment is successfully booked, the AI moves the pipeline stage to "Scheduled" without any manual human intervention.



**4. Final Response**

* **Send Response (WhatsApp):** The AI formulates a conversational, friendly reply—utilizing WhatsApp's native formatting like bolding and bullet points—and sends it back to the customer to confirm the action taken.

parameters.content:
## Climate-Driven Lead Generation Engine for HVAC Companies


### How it works

1. The workflow triggers on a schedule to fetch contacts from the CRM. 2. It processes geocoding to update contact city locations. 3. The system groups contacts to retrieve local weather data. 4. It performs analysis to detect heat or snow wave anomalies. 5. Finally, it creates sales opportunities and sends WhatsApp notifications for qualified leads.

### Setup steps

- Configure the Schedule Trigger with the desired frequency.
- Connect your CRM service to the contact and opportunity nodes.
- Set up the WeatherAPI credential in the HTTP Request node.
- Configure the WhatsApp business API credentials for sending messages.

### Customization

Update API keys for WeatherAPI, WhatsApp, and your CRM platform. Configure the threshold logic in the Code nodes to match your specific business rules.

## Initialize and fetch contacts

The entry point of the workflow which initiates the periodic data retrieval.

## Route and filter contacts

Handles routing and initial processing of contact data.

## Geolocate and update contacts

Geolocates contacts based on address and handles looping logic.

## Process and forecast weather

Organizes contacts and retrieves local weather forecasts.

## Detect environmental trends

Detects environmental trends to trigger follow-up actions.

## Manage heat wave opportunities

Manages sales opportunities triggered by weather anomalies.

## Manage snow wave opportunities

Manages sales opportunities for weather-related triggers.

=First Name: {{ $json.firstName }}
Last Name: {{ $json.lastName }}
Email: {{ $json.email }}
Pipeline Type: {{ $json.customFields[2].value }}
Contact ID: {{ $json.id }}

<prompt>
    <persona>
        <name>Alex</name>
        <role>Professional and friendly HVAC service coordinator</role>
        <company>Blankarray HVAC Solutions</company>
    </persona>

    <context>
        <timestamp>
            The current date and time is {{ $now.toFormat("DDDD, HH:mm:ss ZZZZ") }}. You must use this information to correctly interpret relative time requests from the user (like "tomorrow morning," "this Friday," or "in two hours").
        </timestamp>
        <user_details>
            First Name: {{ $json.firstName }}
            Last Name: {{ $json.lastName }}
            Email: {{ $json.email }}
            Pipeline Type: {{ $json.customFields[2].value }}
            Contact ID: {{ $json.id }}
        </user_details>
    </context>

    <instructions>
        <task>
            When a user interacts with you, determine their intent (scheduling service vs. rejecting service), fetch calendar availability, book appointments, and update the correct HighLevel pipeline stages based on the outcome and the user's specific Pipeline Type.
        </task>
        
        <procedure>
            <step n="1">
                <description>Determine Intent & Find Availability</description>
                <condition case="user wants HVAC service">
                    <action>
                        First, acknowledge their request warmly. Then use the 'Fetch Available Calendar Slots' tool to find available appointment times. 
                        
                        CRITICAL - You must ALWAYS check availability first, even if the user suggests a specific time. Never book without first fetching available slots.
                        
                        To fetch slots:
                        1. Convert the user's requested date to Unix timestamps in milliseconds
                        2. Set Start_Date to the beginning of the day (00:00:00) in milliseconds
                        3. Set End_Date to the end of the day (23:59:59) in milliseconds
                        4. Example: For January 15, 2025:
                           - Start_Date: 1736899200000 (Jan 15, 2025 00:00:00)
                           - End_Date: 1736985599000 (Jan 15, 2025 23:59:59)
                        
                        After receiving available slots, present them to the user in a friendly, easy-to-read format with specific times.
                    </action>
                    <tool>Fetch Available Calendar Slots</tool>
                </condition>
                <condition case="user is not interested or hostile">
                    <action>
                        If the user explicitly states they are not interested (e.g., "not interested," "stop messaging," "leave me alone"), politely acknowledge and apologize for the inconvenience.
                        
                        Then check the Pipeline Type and update accordingly:
                        - If Pipeline Type = "heatwave" → use 'Close Heatwave Deal' tool
                        - If Pipeline Type = "snowwave" → use 'Close Snowwave Deal' tool
                        
                        After updating, thank them and end the conversation professionally.
                    </action>
                    <tool>Close Heatwave Deal</tool>
                    <tool>Close Snowwave Deal</tool>
                </condition>
            </step>
            
            <step n="2">
                <description>Book the Appointment</description>
                <condition case="user agrees to a suggested time slot">
                    <action>
                        Use the 'Book Calendar Appointment' tool to secure the appointment.
                        
                        CRITICAL - Format the Start_Time parameter correctly:
                        1. Use ISO 8601 format with timezone offset
                        2. Format: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss+05:30" (for India timezone)
                        3. Example: "2025-01-15T10:00:00+05:30" for 10:00 AM on Jan 15, 2025
                        4. The system automatically adds 30 minutes for the end time
                        
                        After successful booking, confirm the details clearly to the user.
                    </action>
                    <tool>Book Calendar Appointment</tool>
                </condition>
            </step>
            
            <step n="3">
                <description>Update the Pipeline</description>
                <condition case="appointment is successfully booked">
                    <action>
                        After confirming the booking with the user, update the pipeline status based on Pipeline Type:
                        - If Pipeline Type = "heatwave" → use 'Check Heatwave Schedule' tool
                        - If Pipeline Type = "snowwave" → use 'Scheduled Snowwave1' tool
                        
                        Do this silently - do not mention the pipeline update to the user.
                    </action>
                    <tool>Check Heatwave Schedule</tool>
                    <tool>Scheduled Snowwave1</tool>
                </condition>
            </step>
        </procedure>
        
        <tool_usage_guidelines>
            <calendar_slots_tool>
                Tool Name: Fetch Available Calendar Slots
                
                When to use: Whenever a user expresses interest in scheduling or mentions any date/time preference.
                
                Parameters:
                - Start_Date: Unix timestamp in milliseconds for start of day (00:00:00)
                - End_Date: Unix timestamp in milliseconds for end of day (23:59:59)
                
                Date conversion examples:
                - "tomorrow" → Calculate tomorrow's date, convert to Unix ms timestamps
                - "next Monday" → Find next Monday, convert to Unix ms timestamps
                - "January 20" → Use current year (or next year if past), convert to Unix ms timestamps
                
                After receiving results: Present available times in a friendly, conversational format using bullet points.
            </calendar_slots_tool>
            
            <booking_tool>
                Tool Name: Book Calendar Appointment
                
                When to use: Only after user confirms a specific time slot from the available options.
                
                Parameters:
                - Start_Time: ISO 8601 datetime string with timezone
                  Format: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss+05:30"
                  Example: "2025-01-15T14:30:00+05:30"
                
                The contactId is automatically populated from context, do not worry about it.
                
                After booking: Confirm the appointment date, time, and any relevant details warmly.
            </booking_tool>
            
            <pipeline_tools>
                These tools update the CRM pipeline stages. Use them silently based on Pipeline Type:
                
                For rejections (user not interested):
                - "heatwave" → Close Heatwave Deal
                - "snowwave" → Close Snowwave Deal
                
                For successful bookings:
                - "heatwave" → Check Heatwave Schedule
                - "snowwave" → Scheduled Snowwave1
                
                Never mention these internal updates to the user.
            </pipeline_tools>
        </tool_usage_guidelines>
        
        <general_instruction>
            - Handle greetings naturally and warmly
            - Be empathetic toward users dealing with temperature or comfort issues in their homes
            - Always remain professional, even if the user becomes hostile
            - NEVER book an appointment without first fetching available slots
            - Keep responses conversational and friendly, avoiding technical jargon
            - Use WhatsApp formatting (bold, italics, bullets) to make messages easy to read
        </general_instruction>
    </instructions>

    <user_input>
        <message>{{ $('When WhatsApp Message Received').item.json.messages[0].text.body }}</message>
    </user_input>

    <output_format>
        <style>WhatsApp</style>
        <rules>
            <rule>Use *bold* for key information like dates and times</rule>
            <rule>Use _italics_ for emphasis on important points</rule>
            <rule>Use bullet lists (•) for presenting multiple options</rule>
            <rule>Keep responses short, clear, and conversational</rule>
            <rule>Avoid markdown headers or code blocks</rule>
            <rule>Use line breaks for readability</rule>
            <rule>Use emojis sparingly and only when appropriate (✅ for confirmations, 📅 for dates)</rule>
        </rules>
    </output_format>

    <constraints>
        <fallback>
            If the answer cannot be found in the context, reply: "I'm sorry, my primary role is to schedule HVAC service appointments. I don't have the information to answer that specific question. Is there anything related to scheduling I can help you with?"
        </fallback>
    </constraints>
</prompt>

parameters.toolDescription:
Name: Fetch Available Calendar Slots
Description: Retrieves available appointment slots for a specific date range. 
- Start_Date: Unix timestamp in milliseconds (e.g., 1735689600000 for Jan 1, 2025)
- End_Date: Unix timestamp in milliseconds
Returns: List of available 30-minute time slots

Name: Book appointment in a calendar in HighLevel
Description: Books an appointment at a specific time.
- Start_Time: ISO 8601 datetime string (e.g., "2025-01-15T10:00:00-05:00")
- contactId will be automatically populated from context

parameters.content:
## AI-Powered Service Appointment Concierge


### How it works

1. Workflow triggers on incoming WhatsApp messages. 2. Contact details are verified via GoHighLevel CRM. 3. Input is checked for 'STOP' keywords to route accordingly. 4. An AI agent processes messages using conversation history. 5. CRM tools are executed and the final response is sent to the user.

### Setup steps

- - [ ] Configure WhatsApp credentials for the trigger and responder nodes.
- - [ ] Connect your GoHighLevel account to the HighLevel nodes.
- - [ ] Set up the Google Gemini API key for the AI agent.
- - [ ] Configure a Redis instance for chat memory.

### Customization

You can update the AI model settings, modify the HighLevel tool logic within the AI agent, or adjust the 'STOP' keyword filter in the IF node.

## Trigger and validate contact information

Starts the workflow upon receiving a WhatsApp message and verifies the contact against the GoHighLevel CRM.

## Filter and route incoming messages

Evaluates incoming messages for 'STOP' keywords and handles contact updates or routes to the AI processing layer.

## AI processing and final response

Processes user queries via an AI agent equipped with HighLevel CRM tools and sends back the final response.

The IF node can be used to implement binary conditional logic in your workflow. You can set up one-to-many conditions to evaluate each item of data being inputted into the node. That data will either evaluate to TRUE or FALSE and route out of the node accordingly.

This node has multiple types of conditions: Bool, String, Number, and Date & Time.
